story: Draupadi was born from a sacrificial fire and married all five Pandavas. When Yudhishthira lost her in the dice game, Dushasana dragged her into the court and tried to strip her. She prayed to Krishna, her sari became endless, and she vowed not to tie her hair until it was washed in Dushasana's blood.
belief: She is counted among the Panchakanya, five women of great virtue, and is worshipped as a goddess in South Indian temples. Many see her as the woman who refused to stay silent about injustice.
turns: In popular retellings she laughed at Duryodhana when he fell into a pool at the Pandavas' palace, feeding his hatred. At her swayamvara she openly rejected Karna because of his birth.
facts: She is also called Panchali and Krishnaa.
The Draupadi Amman tradition in Tamil Nadu honours her as a goddess with fire-walking festivals.
Her brother Dhrishtadyumna was born from the same fire.
lessons: Speak against injustice, even in a room of powerful people.
Ask for help; it may come.
Anger can be a fire that cleans or one that burns everything.
more: During exile she had the akshaya patra, a vessel from Surya that never ran out of food.
Krishna called her sakhi, a dear friend.
